gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-malaya: Grandstander draws every letter with one marker-like line and no hairlines anywhere, so headings feel bold and expressive at a glance. Noto Serif Malayalam does the refined part, with gently swelling strokes.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-np-hmo: Loud, expressive letters up top: Grandstander keeps every curve to one thread-like width, while Noto Serif NP Hmong adds a charcoal-like shadow. Up close, its subtle contrast gives the heading something textured to lean on.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-old-uy: Single-weight, outline-like letters give Grandstander its look, while Noto Serif Old Uyghur brings tall, bulb-shaped lowercase bowls with soft shading. Bold up top and restrained below, the two leave each other room.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Grandstander draws in one marker-like line, while Noto Serif Oriya lets its curves run a little heavier than its joins. Dignity from the serif is what anchors the loud heading.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-ottoma: One track width, like a neon sign tube, runs through every Grandstander letter, loud and bold. And Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq feels dignified and classic beside it, swelling only slightly where its bowls are widest.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-sinhal: Grandstander curves carry no stress at all, which keeps its bold, expressive lettering simple. And Noto Serif Sinhala, bookish and refined, would keep paragraphs lively, its stroke weights differing just enough.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-telugu: Noto Serif Telugu has a tempered stroke contrast that neither jolts nor flattens, with lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Grandstander above, with no hairlines at all, supplies the loud, expressive part.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-thai: Noto Serif Thai reads bookish and authoritative, its bodies dominating the line. Give Grandstander generous size so its toothpaste-like single line can show off against the mellow stroke range below.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-tibeta: A ballpoint-pen stroke width defines Grandstander, bold and expressive. Noto Serif Tibetan, authoritative and literary, has a thickness shift you feel more than see, so paragraphs would flow steadily.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-todhri: Diagonals that match the stems in weight give Grandstander its expressive look, while Noto Serif Todhri thickens and thins in gentle steps. Made small, that heading loses its punch, and a large body gets heavy-handed.
